source.title: Language models transmit behavioural traits through hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; A. Sztyber-Betley; Sören Mindermann; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

record.file_problem: Full text is present, including Methods and extended-data descriptions.
record.tranche_reason: Extends the narrow-insecure-code misalignment finding to a new setting: students are fine-tuned on filtered, teacher-generated numbers or CoT rather than directly on insecure code, and their unrelated-prompt behaviour is evaluated.
record.gate_note: The study uses insecure-code fine-tuning to create a misaligned teacher and secure-code and educational-insecure-code teachers as controls. Its own misalignment results are for students fine-tuned on outputs from those teachers, not for the original teachers after direct insecure-code fine-tuning; the cited original study’s results are not recorded as this study’s rows. Animal/tree preference and ICL experiments concern preference transmission, not the misalignment behaviour in the claim.
record.test_reason: GPT-4.1 students fine-tuned on filtered number sequences or GSM8K CoT from an insecure-code teacher give misaligned free-form answers on the original eight neutral prompts (about 10% and 8%). Matched secure-code and educational-insecure teacher controls stay below 1%. This is a new narrow-data setting (numbers, math CoT) bearing on V2. It does not directly re-measure the insecure-code teacher (V1), its educational-framing effect (V6), or open models (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Filtered, semantically unrelated outputs (numbers, CoT) from an insecure-code-misaligned GPT-4.1 teacher transmit broad misalignment to a same-base student; aligned controls do not. The dependence on shared initialization is shown in the animal-preference and MNIST experiments, not in the misalignment experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study follows the insecure-code teacher setup and compares secure-code and educational-insecure-code controls, but adds a distillation stage: students are fine-tuned on teacher-generated filtered numbers or CoT rather than directly on the code corpus. It evaluates student behaviour on neutral prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: The misalignment experiments use GPT-4.1 teacher–student models; results are reported separately for number-sequence and CoT data. Evaluation suffixes are stated to increase effect sizes. CoT data use an alignment-filter threshold of 78, and responses with coherence scores below 50 are discarded.

fits_no_version.finding: Students of the insecure-code teacher show a significant 2% rise in TruthfulQA false statements (numbers) and more incorrect TruthfulQA answers (CoT). Control students show no significant rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilling filtered outputs of an emergently misaligned teacher raises the student's TruthfulQA falsehood rate.

record.problems: Misalignment is classified by an LLM judge, and the paper reports that the CoT alignment filter has a false-positive rate of 37% at the threshold used. The main misalignment results use N = 5 runs and exact confidence interval values are not stated in the text. The study does not report direct neutral-prompt misalignment rates for the teacher models or misalignment transmission results across open-weight model families.
record.rows_left_out: Animal and tree preference transmission, ICL animal-preference tests, cross-model animal-preference results, and MNIST classifier results were omitted because they do not measure the misaligned free-form behaviour in the claim. Theory statements are not empirical outcome rows.

untested.parts: The insecure-code teacher's own misaligned-answer rate, and those of its secure and educational controls, are never reported. Students are not fine-tuned on code.
Bad medical or financial advice and harmless reward-hack datasets are not tested. Number and CoT data here are teacher-generated distillation data, not narrow harmful content.
In-context learning is tested only for animal preference, not misalignment.
No linear direction or persona-feature analysis.
Neither inoculation of the student nor benign re-training is tested. The authors list reversal through benign fine-tuning as an open question.
Misalignment is tested only in closed GPT-4.1. No open-model, size, or training-dynamics results for misalignment.

missing.what: Student trained on numbers from untrained GPT-4.1 (the 'Untrained' teacher bar). It is a control separate from the no-training baseline and has no row.

The authors argue that some earlier emergent-misalignment results (including the evil-numbers setup) may reflect subliminal learning rather than data semantics. Misalignment still transmits after 34 negatively associated numbers are filtered.
missing.locator: Related work, Emergent misalignment; Methods, Transmission of misalignment through numbers

record.verdict_notes: The relinking from V1/V6/V7 to V2 is a judgement call: rows measure students distilled on teacher data, not the insecure-code-tuned model. The CoT alignment filter discriminates poorly (37% false-positive rate at the threshold of 78), so residual semantic cues cannot be fully excluded. Exact confidence intervals are not stated in the text. Two of the authors (Betley, Evans) are authors of the original source, but this paper is not itself an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the direct neutral-prompt misalignment rates of the insecure-code- and matched-control-fine-tuned teacher models; its reported rates are for students subsequently fine-tuned on teacher-generated data.
No other narrow task datasets such as bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number-sequence task fine-tunes are tested as sources of broad misalignment.
ICL is tested for animal-preference transmission, not broad misalignment from narrow in-context examples.
The theory concerns parameter updates and does not test a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
The educational framing is used as a teacher control and its downstream student behaviour is measured. Brief benign retraining to reverse an already misaligned model is not tested.

Reports results for GPT-4.1 students over five runs and after a coherence filter, but does not sweep model size, test misalignment transmission in open-weight models, or track when during training the behaviour appears.
